articles.title: Antonio Brown used an offensive, derogatory slur against Caleb Williams after a locker room video with Case Keenum went viral
articles.summary: This is the second time that Antonio Brown has taken a social media dig at Caleb Williams.
articles.body: This is the second time that Antonio Brown has taken a social media dig at Caleb Williams.A viral locker room clip showed Williams standing in the background while Case Keenum gave his Chicago Bears vs. Philadelphia Eagles 27-7 winning speech. Brown took a screenshot of the clip and added a cheap caption directed at the young quarterback.The X post included an offensive, homophobic, derogatory slur. For the second time, Brown called Williams “Fa*got of the Week.” Back in 2025, Brown labeled Williams “Fa*got of the Day” after a viral tweet claimed Williams wasn't interested in girls as a kid because he was too locked into football.Antonio Brown’s comment follows a viral video of Caleb Williams in the locker room with Case KeenumCaleb Williams suffered a Grade 2 hamstring injury in the Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. He did not play against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 3. Case Keenum served as his backup QB. Keenum led the team to a win over the Eagles, throwing for 247 yards and 2 touchdowns and scoring a rushing touchdown.Following the victory, Keenum received the game ball in the locker room celebration. While Keenum gave his memorable speech, Williams stood behind him in a bathrobe, hands folded and a bright smile on his face. Antonio Brown took a screenshot of that unusual moment and posted it on his X.The former Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver used a homophobic, derogatory slur and labeled Williams his “Fa*got of the Week.” There is no end to the kind of weird, adulterated posts Brown showcases on his X account. But this one stood apart from the others, especially because of the offensive nature of the insult.Brown has previously used provocative and controversial labels while targeting athletes and public figures on his X account.Williams has not responded to the post. He may treat it the same way he treated his several other AI-generated posts. One that had him crying on the field after he chipped his nail polish. The other when he posed provocatively for an NFL rivalry jersey photoshoot.Just that it was Case Keenum’s big night, and it somehow looked like Caleb Williams wanted to own it. Yes, it’s his team. Yes, Keenum’s a backup. But who plays on the gridiron and wins the battles for the franchise - matters the most.Caleb Williams’ nonstop controversy overshadows Case Keenum’s victoryThe 38-year-old quarterback Case Keenum returned to the gridiron after 1,009 days. He played as he’d never played before. This was his one chance to prove his worth. He helped beat the Jalen Hurts-led Philadelphia Eagles by a tormenting 27-7 score.When it was his time to share his joy with the team that helped him win, an injured [almost] franchise quarterback snatched his spotlight.When Caleb Williams could have easily stood in front of Keenum, listening to his victory speech like the rest of the team, he chose to stand right behind him - probably knowing for a fact that he was being recorded. And that’s how he became the hero behind the actual hero.He took the footage to the next level. As though Keenum was playing for him, not his team. Anyhow, the clip knew it would go viral. Caleb probably knew it would go viral, too.And viral-news-hungry gossipmongers like Antonio Brown also knew it would look great on their feed. And that’s what he did. He made the Williams’ story look louder and brighter than expected. Clearly surpassing Case Keenum’s victory case.Anyhow, Chicago improved its season record from 1-1 to 2-1. But Caleb took the cake, even without being on the gridiron… he got all the footage, just by being behind Case.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce is most likely one season away from retirement; his real estate portfolio suggests he is already planning the next chapter
articles.summary: Travis Kelce signed a one-year, $12 million deal with the Chiefs in March, and the contract is built so he can leave after this season.
articles.body: Travis Kelce signed a one-year, $12 million deal with the Chiefs in March, and the contract is built so he can leave after this season. He has not said he will. His property buying suggests he is at least preparing. Reports say Kelce closed on a $5.35 million Ohio lakefront estate about three weeks before he re-signed. Neither purchase proves anything on its own, but the timing is hard to ignore. Add the roughly $6 million Kansas mansion he already owns, and the 36-year-old looks like a player lining up where life goes after football.Is Travis Kelce one season away from retiring?Not officially. Kelce has made no announcement about 2027. The paperwork, though, leaves the door open. His 2026 deal pays $12 million and can reach $15 million. Some early reports called it a three-year, $54.7 million contract, but two of those years exist only on paper to spread out the salary cap cost. Sports Illustrated reported that the setup lets the Chiefs release him after June 1 if he retires. CBS Sports noted the contract is built for him to decide by June 2027.The football case for another year is real. Kelce led Kansas City with 76 catches and 851 yards last season and made his 11th straight Pro Bowl. Kelce turns 37 on Monday. He already holds the franchise records for catches, yards and touchdowns. But the Chiefs missed the playoffs for the first time since 2014, and that kind of result makes any veteran count his remaining seasons. Last November, Kelce said, "I want to give the Chiefs a good opportunity, whether I come back or not." He came back, and the same logic applies again next summer.What does Travis Kelce's real estate say about life after football?The Ohio purchase says the most. TMZ reported that Kelce bought the Bratenahl estate on March 2, months before his wedding to Taylor Swift. The Wall Street Journal said it first listed at $5.99 million. The 21,000-square-foot home, called Moyenage, was built in 1895 and sits on about 3.5 acres along Lake Erie. It is a Tudor-style mansion near Cleveland, in the state where Kelce grew up. Three weeks later, he re-signed with Kansas City.Compare that with Leawood. The Kansas mansion cost about $6 million and covers 17,000 square feet on roughly 3.5 acres, with tennis and pickleball courts and a mini-golf course. Reports link its heavy privacy to his relationship with Swift. Reports are unclear on whether he still owns his first Kansas City home, a $995,000 purchase from 2019. Leawood reads like a home built around football and fame. Bratenahl reads like one built for a slower life.One count puts the value of his three homes at $12.35 million. Together with Swift's properties, the couple's portfolio is reportedly worth about $157 million. So a career after the NFL is not a money problem. It is a question of how he spends the time. New Heights, the podcast he hosts with Jason, is an obvious answer. Jason, now retired, owns a three-unit rental house in Cleveland, so Ohio real estate is already a family habit. Kelce has not spoken publicly about why he bought the Ohio home, so the link to retirement is a reading of the timeline, not a confirmed plan.Kelce has until June 2027 to decide. The Ohio house is already bought.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce receive $140 gifts as NFL brothers gush over special delivery
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark found a way to surprise two of the NFL’s most recognisable brothers, and Travis and Jason Kelce made no secret of how much they appreciated
articles.body: Caitlin Clark found a way to surprise two of the NFL’s most recognisable brothers, and Travis and Jason Kelce made no secret of how much they appreciated it. The Indiana Fever star sent the Kelce brothers pairs of her Nike Caitlin 1 signature shoes, giving them a chance to check out the sneakers up close during the latest episode of New Heights. Travis received the “Sea of Red” colourway, a nod to his Kansas City Chiefs connection, while Jason got the “Warning Code” version. Their reactions quickly turned into a lively celebration of Clark, her growing signature line and the personal touch behind the gift.Travis and Jason Kelce show off Caitlin Clark shoesTravis Kelce was particularly impressed by the red design he received. As the brothers opened their packages, the Chiefs tight end immediately pointed out the familiar initials on the shoes.“I know you see the CC right there,” Travis said.The “Sea of Red” design caught his attention because of its Kansas City-inspired colours. Travis also revealed that he had already seen Chiefs head coach Andy Reid receive his own pair before the Kelce brothers got theirs.“I hope mine are in the mail!” Travis recalled thinking after seeing Reid’s sneakers.His patience eventually paid off. Travis praised the shoe’s appearance and construction, describing it as a mix of style and function.“This is the best. I f---ing love kicks and I love Caitlin Clarks,” Travis said, calling the red colourway “so icy.”He also highlighted the shoe’s modern look and the blend of yellow and red.“Absolutely fire...you can’t go wrong with these things,” he continued, adding, “I understand why she’s dropping, like, 25 and 11 on everybody. Makes me wanna go out and shoot from half court.”Caitlin Clark’s Nike shoes impress the Kelce brothersJason Kelce had his own enthusiastic response to the “Warning Code” colourway. The former Philadelphia Eagles centre focused on the design details and admitted that he would have loved to own a pair during his playing career.Jason called the sneakers “freaking awesome” and said he appreciated “all the designs” and “details in them.”He also thanked Clark directly, saying he “could not be more happy that you sent these” and joking that he wished he “would’ve had these when I was trying to dunk.”Travis also used the moment to congratulate Clark on her signature footwear line. The WNBA star previously appeared on New Heights in December 2025, making the latest exchange a natural continuation of their connection.“Nike and Caitlin herself absolutely knocked it out of the park,” Travis said.Andy Reid had received his shoes roughly a week earlier and shared his own reaction.“Appreciate you girl,” Reid said to Clark in a video showing off his pair of the sneakers. “Caitlin, I love the colors man, I love these things.”The playful unboxing gave fans another glimpse of the connection between Clark and the Kelce family, while also putting the spotlight on Clark’s growing presence beyond the basketball court.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “Match made in heaven”: Patrick Mahomes’ favorite coffee company raises $18 million in total funding as Throne Sport Coffee expands to 20,000 retail locations
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes’ longtime morning coffee habit has become a multi-million-dollar business opportunity.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes’ longtime morning coffee habit has become a multi-million-dollar business opportunity. The Kansas City Chiefs QB-backed Throne Sport Coffee has now gladly reportedly secured $18 million in total funding. It has also rapidly expanded its retail footprint, with the brand targeting more than 20,000 locations across the U.S.For Mahomes, the beverage company represents a personal business investment. The three-time Super Bowl champion has openly spoken about his love for coffee. He picked up the habit during his early days with the Kansas City Chiefs. This habit eventually sparked his interest in the ready-to-drink, up-and-coming coffee market.Patrick Mahomes’ Throne Sport Coffee inceptionThrone Sport Coffee brand launched in 2024. Patrick Mahomes became the brand’s lead investor alongside beverage industry veteran Michael Fedele. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback’s involvement goes beyond attaching his massively established name to the product.ESPN reported that Mahomes is the company’s No. 2 stakeholder. He has been involved in product development, including testing and providing feedback on the coffee. So much for a perennial coffee lover.The two-time NFL MVP’s coffee routine reportedly dates back to his rookie season in 2017. Long team meetings with the Kansas City Chiefs helped him develop a regular coffee-consuming habit. His intense interest ultimately led him to Throne Sport Coffee.“It actually started in my first year in the NFL,” Mahomes told CNBC. “I started drinking coffee a lot, just being in a lot of meetings. And I really just fell in love with it. You know, it started first as a functional thing. And then I really fell in love with just the taste and trying to make sure that what I was putting into my body was good.And so I was trying to get away from drinking all the sugary, different types of coffees that you could drink.And I was really into just black coffee, which is what I was drinking on a day-to-day basis. And so whenever Michael Fedele and Throne Sport Coffee came to me and said they had a ready-to-go, healthy cold brew coffee drink, it was like a match made in heaven.”The brand markets ready-to-drink coffee designed exclusively for customers looking for both caffeine and functional ingredients.“It was really cool to see that I got to be part of the very beginning of the tasting part of the B vitamins, the BCAAs, the electrolytes going into it and something that I could drink on a day-to-day basis. And I know that it's good stuff that's going into my body,” Mahomes added.Patrick Mahomes’ investment strategyPatrick Mahomes genuinely values his partnerships with brands including State Farm, Adidas, Doritos, T-Mobile, Subway, Coors Light, Invisalign, and Throne Sport Coffee. His relationship with Throne Sport Coffee is a little different because he’s one of the lead investors there, and he strongly believes in the product.The product is a convenient option for both athletes and everyday consumers, specifically because it is ready to drink and contains 150 milligrams of natural caffeine. The quarterback believes the product could be a good everyday coffee choice.Mahomes has had many business opportunities come his way, but he carefully chose to work with companies and products that he truly believed in. He values the people behind those businesses. He prefers partnerships that are built on long-term relationships and everlasting trust.This personalized approach extends beyond investments to his teammates, charitable work, and other areas of life. He wants to surround himself with people he believes are good and genuinely want to make a positive impact on the world.Patrick Mahomes’ Throne Sport Coffee valuation and investor detailsAccording to Dealroom, Throne Sport Coffee has a $25 to $50 million valuation, a team of fewer than 100, and $10 to $50 million in total funding.The brand reached a massive milestone in February 2026, announcing a $10 million funding round, as per Food Business News.Throne Sport Coffee raised $10 million in a Series A round. The funds will support the brand’s next growth stage, including expanded distribution, field sales, and marketing.The company has raised a total of $18 million, according to Drew Fallon, Co-Founder and CEO of Iris Finance.The brand’s investors include professional athletes, sports executives, beverage-industry veterans, and other business founders.The brand offers several ready-to-drink varieties, including mocha java, salted caramel, mint mocha, French vanilla, and black. Its Coffee PLUS+ formula comes with caffeine, B vitamins, electrolytes, and BCAAs.Patrick Mahomes’ Throne Sport Coffee retail expansionThe brand’s fundraising helps its distribution network to grow. Food Business News reported that Throne Sport Coffee had reached roughly 7,000 retail locations by February 2026. It was nearly 5,000 in January 2025.The brand has since expanded to more than 20,000 retail locations, growing through major retailers and convenience chains such as Kroger, CVS, Whole Foods, Casey’s, QuikTrip, and Sheetz, as reported by Boardroom.That expansion comes as it debuts its new Patrick Mahomes-led “Better Fuel for Every You” campaign, part of a larger push to bring functional coffee further into the mainstream.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ mom Randi Mahomes shares proud moment from special family celebration
articles.summary: For a family accustomed to celebrating Super Bowl victories and NFL milestones, one of the Mahomes family’s latest happy moments had nothing to do with
articles.body: For a family accustomed to celebrating Super Bowl victories and NFL milestones, one of the Mahomes family’s latest happy moments had nothing to do with football. Randi Mahomes proudly marked daughter Mia Randall’s first high school homecoming, sharing a glimpse of the teenager dressed up for the special night. The post quickly attracted warm reactions from family and fans, giving followers a rare look at a more personal side of the Mahomes family. For Randi, the occasion was another reminder of how quickly her youngest daughter is growing up.Randi Mahomes celebrates Mia Randall’s homecomingRandi shared a photo from Mia’s big night on Instagram, capturing the teenager in a blue dress as she stood beside her mother. Randi held a bouquet featuring a white ribbon marked “Hoco 2026,” adding another personal touch to the celebration.Her caption summed up the excitement in just a few words: “Homecoming 2026 for my Mia!”The post soon filled with supportive messages. Mia’s brother Jackson Mahomes was among those who reacted, writing, “So pretty!!!” Fans also joined in, with several congratulating Mia and sharing their own memories of watching children grow up.One follower wrote, “Have a great time you deserve it, and so beautiful too.”Another added, “You both look wonderful. Congratulations to Mia and have Fun.”The response showed that the moment resonated beyond football. It was not about Patrick Mahomes’ latest performance or a Chiefs victory. Instead, it was about a mother celebrating a milestone in her daughter’s life.Patrick Mahomes’ sister Mia enters a new chapterMia, born in July 2011, has grown up around the spotlight because of her famous older brother. Yet she has also developed an identity of her own as a young athlete, with basketball, volleyball and soccer among the sports she has played.She has also been a familiar face around the Kansas City Chiefs. Mia has supported Patrick at games and was present during celebrations following several of his Super Bowl victories, giving her a close view of some of the biggest moments of his career.Randi previously shared her emotions as Mia prepared to leave middle school behind.“Mia is the BEST! Class of 2029.”She also wrote, “It’s hard to believe my baby girl is headed to high school. Watching @miablissss grow into such a smart, strong, and beautiful young lady has been the sweetest journey. Time, please slow down!! I’m so proud of you, Mia, and can’t wait to see all the amazing things you’ll do next.”Now, with Mia celebrating homecoming, that next chapter is already underway.For Randi, the photographs capture more than a dressed-up teenager. They mark another step in watching her youngest child grow into her own person, away from the enormous shadow of the Mahomes football legacy.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How Travis Kelce spends his fortune: $6M mansion, $1.4M car collection, $400K Rolls-Royce and $20K sneakers
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has built an impressive fortune through his NFL career, but his spending habits reveal another side of the Kansas City Chiefs star.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has built an impressive fortune through his NFL career, but his spending habits reveal another side of the Kansas City Chiefs star. From rare sneakers and luxury watches to high-end cars and multimillion-dollar homes, Kelce has developed a taste for statement purchases. His collection reflects his interests as much as his wealth. Some of his biggest expenses are tied to fashion, while others offer a glimpse into how the three-time Super Bowl champion enjoys life away from football. Here is a closer look at some of Travis Kelce’s most expensive possessions and purchases reported by Prestige in 2024.Travis Kelce’s luxury cars and real estateCars are among the biggest expenses in Kelce’s lifestyle. His collection was reported to be worth around USD 1.4 million, with nine vehicles ranging from classic American cars to luxury SUVs.His Rolls-Royce Ghost was listed at about USD 400,000, making it one of the standout vehicles in his garage. He also owns a 1970 Chevrolet Chevelle, valued at roughly USD 149,000. The vintage car gained extra attention after Kelce was seen driving Taylor Swift in it in 2023.Kelce has also invested heavily in property. One of his notable purchases was a Kansas mansion reportedly worth USD 6 million. The 17,000-square-foot home sits inside a gated community in Leawood and includes six bedrooms and six bathrooms.His property holdings also include a seven-bedroom Kansas City home purchased for about USD 995,000 in 2019, along with an Orlando condo valued at approximately USD 355,000.Travis Kelce’s expensive sneakers and fashion collectionIf there is one category that clearly reflects Kelce’s personality, it is sneakers. The NFL star reportedly owns more than 300 pairs, including rare and highly valuable designs.Among his most expensive pairs are Dior Air Jordan 1s, reportedly valued at around USD 20,000. He also owns the Air Mag Marty McFly sneakers, which cost about USD 10,000. Kelce has previously explained how his love for sneakers began with a pair inspired by Back to the Future.“I am a big sneaker fan. So, I had to have the Marty McFlys, the Back to the Future, the Nike Airbags were the first purchase of kicks that I got. I knew I wanted them ever since saw them self-tie themselves on McFly’s feet.”His luxury taste extends beyond footwear. Kelce has been seen wearing Rolex watches, designer clothing and premium accessories from brands including Louis Vuitton, Bottega Veneta, Celine and Amiri.He also reportedly spent about USD 1 million on a Super Bowl suite for family and friends during Super Bowl LVIII.“I’m not really doing much different other than just counting how much money I’m spending on this damn Super Bowl for family and friends to come. Just making sure I’m on top of those finances and losing all this money.”The purchases show how Kelce has turned his NFL success into a lifestyle filled with cars, property, fashion and collectibles.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, Browns' QB Situation Amid 2-1 Start
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns are reportedly ready to stick by Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback after a 2-1 start to the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns are reportedly ready to stick by Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback after a 2-1 start to the 2026 season.

ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi reported Thursday that "while team sources indicated that Watson's performance through three games hasn't convinced the Browns to consider Watson the long-term answer, Cleveland's surprising start has shifted the conversation inside the building to whether the 31-year-old passer and the Browns can build short-term momentum."

Oyefusi added, "Team sources said Watson's ability to move past negative plays and stretches instead of compounding them has stood out."

The Biggest Disappointments of NFL Season So Far ☹️

Following a season-opening loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, Watson has led the Browns to back-to-back victories at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and against the visiting Carolina Panthers.

That marked Watson's first time since 2023 winning consecutive games in Cleveland, where in 2022 he signed a fully-guaranteed five-year, $230 million deal for which he has been mostly unavailable.

Watson made his return for the last year of that contract, and the first time since tearing his Achilles tendon in 2024, after beating out Shedeur Sanders for the Week 1 starting job in training camp.

ESPN's Ian Rapoport reported after the season-opening loss to the Jaguars the Browns planned to re-evaluate the QB1 position after Week 2.

The Browns turned again to Watson as starter for Week 3, after which Rapoport reported on NFL Network Watson had played well enough the Browns no longer wanted to "go week-to-week" in terms of which quarterback would be starting.

Sanders still looks set to stick around in Cleveland, especially given the status of Watson's expiring contract. Cleveland.com's Mary Kay Cabot reported last weekend the Browns have no plans to trade either Sanders or Dillon Gabriel by the Nov. 10 deadline.

With Gabriel currently on IR with a back injury, Sanders will be slated to back up Watson Thursday night against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Watson is heading into the matchup having so far completed 68.3 percent of his passes for 587 yards with five touchdowns and an interception to go along with 105 rushing yards in three games.

articles.title: Terrell Owens Claps Back at Cris Carter, Deion Sanders Weighs In as Video, Comments Go Viral
articles.summary: Never one to shy away from a discussion, Terrell Owens has put himself in a social media battle with Cris Carter relating back to comments the latter made after a playoff game from January 1998.
articles.body:
Never one to shy away from a discussion, Terrell Owens has put himself in a social media battle with Cris Carter relating back to comments the latter made after a playoff game from January 1998.

On the latest episode of his Fully Loaded podcast, Carter said he "hasn't missed out" on anything by not talking to Owens in response to Owens saying he "can't stand" the Minnesota Vikings legend.

That prompted Owens to clap back in a post on X by quote tweeting the video of Carter's comments and writing he hasn't "missed out on anything not talking to you either."

Their bickering caught the attention of Colorado head coach Deion Sanders, who had plenty of experience from his playing days going up against both Owens and Carter, and urged them to "replace the hate with Love & respect" toward each other.

The origin of the situation appears to stem from Owens recounting a story in which a reporter told him after a Vikings playoff game against the San Francisco 49ers in January 1998 that Carter said Minnesota's cornerbacks "made a mediocre receiver look like a Pro Bowler."

It's not clear which 49ers receiver Carter was said to be describing as mediocre. J.J. Stokes was the one who led the team in receiving yards with 101 in the game. Owens, who was in his second NFL season at that point, had four catches for 49 yards and one touchdown.

San Francisco won the game 38-22 to advance to the NFC Championship Game.

articles.title: Bears’ Ben Johnson keeps it cryptic on Caleb Williams, QB situation for Week 4 vs. Jets
articles.summary: Caleb Williams has not missed a game since the Chicago Bears selected him with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. However, an unfortunate hamstrin...
articles.body:
Caleb Williams has not missed a game since the Chicago Bears selected him with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. However, an unfortunate hamstring injury has now put the quarterback's availability in question, while head coach Ben Johnson has remained cautious and somewhat vague when discussing the status of his star signal-caller.

The Bears are set to host the New York Jets in Week 4. According to Kevin Fishbain of The Athletic, Williams will not participate in Wednesday's walkthrough , Johnson confirmed, though the coach noted that the quarterback is "getting better every single day." Fishbain also reported that the Bears have not made a decision regarding their starting quarterback.

Williams suffered a non-contact hamstring injury while scrambling during the fourth quarter of Chicago's Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings . The injury forced him to leave the field on a cart and immediately raised concerns about his availability moving forward.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Medical evaluations later confirmed that Williams suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain. He was subsequently ruled out for Week 3 against the Philadelphia Eagles , ending the first stretch of his NFL career in which he had started 36 consecutive regular-season games.

Before the injury, Williams had also become the first Bears quarterback to start every game in consecutive seasons since the NFL expanded to a 16-game schedule in 1978.

Doctors initially projected a recovery period of approximately three to four weeks, putting Williams' potential return around the middle of October. That timeline means the Bears are likely to remain cautious as they determine when their franchise quarterback is ready to return.

Before suffering the injury, Williams had gotten off to a promising start under Johnson. Across his first two starts, he completed 32 of 55 pass attempts for 407 yards, two passing touchdowns, and one interception.

However, for now, his status remains a week-to-week situation as the Bears' medical staff continues monitoring his recovery and progress toward a full return.

articles.title: Should the Raiders trade for Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison Jr.?
articles.summary: Should the Las Vegas Raiders trade for Arizona Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison Jr.?
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders are off to a dreamy 3-0 start . Everything is currently firing on all cylinders. Veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins is managing the offense while rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza sits and learns behind the scenes.

One of the Raiders' priorities will be to acquire a true No. 1 receiver for Mendoza. With the Raiders at 3-0, could GM John Spytek consider making a deal near the trade deadline?

The young Raiders will be careful with giving up future picks, as they are still a rebuilding squad despite the 3-0 start. One opportunity that could be worth exploring resides in the NFC. Are the Arizona Cardinals willing to trade underperforming wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr.?

Billed as an elite prospect coming out of Ohio State, Harrison has come nowhere near meeting the predraft hype. The fourth overall selection in 2024 seriously regressed last season as a sophomore compared to his rookie year. This season, he's registered four receptions and zero touchdowns in three appearances.

The Raiders recently lost Jack Bech for an undetermined amount of time due to a serious forearm injury. Bech has been placed on IR . His injury makes a thin Raiders depth chart at receiver even thinner.

With a decision needed this coming offseason on his fifth-year option, the rebuilding Cardinals could be looking to trade Harrison. Trade activity is starting to pick up around the league, with the Pittsburgh Steelers sending cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys on Wednesday evening. The Raiders should at least explore what it'd take to acquire Harrison and give him a much-needed fresh start.

articles.title: NFL Thursday Night Football best bets Week 4
articles.summary: Best bets for TNF Week 4 between the Steelers and Browns.
articles.body:
Week 4 of the NFL season gets Thursday night underway with the Pittsburgh Steelers taking on the Cleveland Browns . There are several player props worth targeting in this AFC North matchup, with Jaylen Warren , Denzel Boston, Pat Freiermuth , and Harold Fannin Jr. all presenting intriguing opportunities.

Sep 13, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren (30) runs during the fourth quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Jaylen Warren over 59.5 rushing yards is one of the best bets to consider Thursday night. Warren has already rushed for 216 yards on 38 carries through three games, averaging an impressive 5.7 yards per carry.

Cleveland has allowed 120.3 rushing yards per game through the first three weeks, creating a favorable matchup for Warren. His efficiency has also been one of the biggest positives for Pittsburgh's offense early this season.

If Warren continues to receive the majority of Pittsburgh's rushing workload, 60 yards is a very attainable number.

That big-play ability makes this number particularly appealing. Boston doesn't need a massive target total to clear 35.5 yards, as one or two explosive receptions could put him over the number.

Pittsburgh's defense has been solid against the pass, but Boston has already demonstrated the ability to produce regardless of matchup.

The rookie tight end has shown the ability to pile up receptions, and his role gives him a path to reaching five catches even without a huge yardage performance.

articles.title: NFL Legend Kurt Warner Posts Tutorial Video for Young QBs
articles.summary: Kurt Warner is once again using his experience to help the next generation of quarterbacks avoid one of the most common mistakes in the passing game. The for...
articles.body:
Kurt Warner is once again using his experience to help the next generation of quarterbacks avoid one of the most common mistakes in the passing game. The former NFL quarterback recently shared a tutorial explaining how young QBs can improve their execution on double-move routes.

Warner's lesson focuses on what quarterbacks should do after initially looking toward the receiver during the route. Instead of keeping their eyes locked on the wideout after recognizing that he has created separation, quarterbacks should quickly check the free safety or return their vision to the middle of the field before resetting their feet.

That brief adjustment can make a major difference in the timing of the throw. When a receiver executes a double move, he still needs time to complete the route and regain his full speed, meaning a quarterback who rushes the throw can release the ball before his target is ready to accelerate downfield.

The former NFL star also explained how quarterbacks can fall into the trap of watching a receiver for too long after seeing him win the route. While the initial reaction may be to deliver the ball immediately, keeping the eyes on the receiver can cause the quarterback to rush his mechanics and ultimately miss a potential explosive play.

NFL Icon Kurt Warner Shares Tutorial Video for Young Quarterbacks

Warner recently shared a video that'll help young quarterbacks improve their game and do away with their mistakes . This can be seen in a post he made on X.

Resetting the feet while briefly looking away gives the receiver an opportunity to finish the route before the quarterback returns his attention to the target. Once the quarterback looks back, he can better judge the receiver's speed and position, allowing him to make a more accurate throw and maximize the opportunity created by the route.

Warner's tutorial offers a simple reminder that successful quarterback play often depends on small technical details. For young passers and coaches looking to improve, mastering footwork, eye discipline and timing on double moves could turn missed opportunities into some of the biggest plays on the field.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes, Chiefs Continue Climb in NFL Power Rankings After 3-0 Start
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs have continued their rise in NFL power rankings after opening the 2026 season with three straight victories. Their...
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs have continued their rise in NFL power rankings after opening the 2026 season with three straight victories. Their latest win over the Miami Dolphins further strengthened the perception that Kansas City has returned to the upper tier of the league.

The Chiefs defeated Miami 24-10 on the road, completing another steady performance without needing to produce an overwhelming offensive showing. Kansas City controlled the game effectively, while its defense prevented the Dolphins from generating enough momentum to make the contest particularly close.

Mahomes has been central to the team's strong beginning, looking increasingly comfortable as the offense finds its rhythm. Through three games, he has thrown for 812 yards and seven touchdowns with two interceptions, while also contributing a rushing touchdown.

The emergence of Kenneth Walker III has added another important element to the offense. His production on the ground has given Kansas City a more balanced attack, allowing the Chiefs to create opportunities without placing the entire burden on Mahomes and the passing game.

Patrick Mahomes and Kansas City Chiefs Rise to Third Place in Latest NFL Power Rankings

Mahomes and company have taken the third spot in the latest power rankings. This is detailed more in an analysis by Nate Taylor for ESPN.

Week 3 result: Beat the Dolphins 24-10 Week 3 ranking: 4 Fantasy surprise: RB Kenneth Walker III Most fantasy owners knew Walker was a good choice, especially after his impressive postseason run to help the Seahawks win the Super Bowl. But not even the Chiefs could have expected this level of production from Walker, who has the second-most total fantasy points at RB this season. He has already produced 442 scrimmage yards and four total touchdowns. Walker is the first player in franchise history to have two games with a rushing and receiving touchdown within the first three weeks, per ESPN Research.

The Chiefs now face one of their most intriguing tests of the young season when they visit the unbeaten Las Vegas Raiders . Oddly enough, given the resources thrown at the position, defensive tackle has become a strength once again. The trade for Dexter Lawrence and the acquisition of Jonathan Allen have reverberated through the team on a number of levels. Aside from the rest of the team sensing the "all-in" mentality from a hyper-aggressive offseason (at least by this team's standards), these two have brought locker room leadership and on-field production. Last year's IDL starters, T.J. Slaton Jr. and B.J. Hill (both still good players), are now rotational guys, which makes this front formidable, as it was back in 2021 when they had Hill, DJ Reader, Larry Ogunjobi and others on the inside. articles.title: The NFL May Be Approaching the Breaking Point of the 17-Game Season
articles.summary: When the league expanded the schedule in 2021, it went from 16 to 17 games came with one fewer preseason game. Five years later, it is fair to wonder whether...
articles.body:
What it may not have fully accounted for was everything that comes with asking the same basic roster to survive a 17-game season.

When the league expanded the schedule in 2021, it made the first change to the regular season since 1978. The move from 16 to 17 games came with one fewer preseason game, but the basic structure of an NFL roster remained largely familiar. Teams still build around a 53-man roster and, under current rules, generally dress 47 or 48 players on game day.

Five years later, it is fair to wonder whether the 17-game season has outgrown the roster designed to survive it.

One additional game doesn't sound dramatic.

It is only 60 more minutes of football, after all. Except it isn't.

Another game means another week of practice, another week of players managing existing injuries, another round of collisions, and another opportunity for something that was merely sore in September to become something far more significant by December.

The postseason makes the equation even more demanding. A team reaching the Super Bowl can play as many as 21 combined regular-season and playoff games. That is a long way from the NFL schedule players once navigated.

The league partially compensated for the 17-game season by reducing the preseason from four games to three. That limits some unnecessary August exposure, particularly for established starters. But preseason snaps and regular-season snaps aren't interchangeable.

The 17th game is different from the preseason game that disappeared when the NFL expanded the schedule. Nobody is protecting starters in Week 18 because the result doesn't count. For some teams, that game decides whether there will even be a Week 19.

The 17-Game Season Has Put More Pressure on 53 Players

The NFL didn't suddenly become an injury-plagued sport when the schedule expanded. That's too easy an argument to make, and probably the wrong one.

Look instead at what happens to the bottom half of a roster over four months.

An offensive lineman who was signed to play guard may end up at center. The swing tackle gets thrown into the lineup. A defensive back gets promoted from the practice squad on Saturday and is covering kicks on Sunday. By late in the year, teams are signing players who weren't part of the original plan at all.

Some of that happened when there were 16 games, too. The difference with a 17-game season is that there is now another week to get through before the playoffs even begin.

And 53 isn't really 53 on Sunday. The game-day limit leaves coaches with 47 or 48 active players. Take out the specialists, backup quarterback, and players whose primary jobs are on special teams, and the available depth gets eaten up quickly.

That's one reason offensive line versatility has become so valuable. A reserve who can play center and both guard spots solves more problems than a player who can only do one thing. It isn't necessarily because he's the better player. Sometimes he's simply the player a 53-man roster makes easier to keep.

The 17-game season gives teams one more week for those compromises to catch up with them.

The 17-Game Season Could Change the Value of a Backup

Maybe the bigger adjustment needs to happen before anybody gets hurt.

NFL teams have already done this with defensive linemen. They rotate. A starting defensive tackle doesn't need to play every snap. Nobody looks at 45 snaps instead of 65 and assumes he's been demoted.

Teams decided a fresh defensive lineman can be more useful than squeezing every possible snap out of the starter.

Running backs have gone through something similar. The days when every team wanted one back, carrying the ball 350 times, are mostly gone.

That thinking is harder to apply elsewhere.

Nobody is voluntarily sitting a healthy left tackle for two series in a close game. Quarterbacks certainly aren't rotating. If a receiver is clearly better than the guy behind him, coaches want him on the field.

That's understandable. Coaches aren't paid to have the healthiest roster in January. They have to win the game in front of them first.

But over a 17-game season, those snaps add up.

At some point, having a capable second player at a position may need to become more than protection against an injury. It may become part of how teams get through the year.

There is a problem with saying the NFL should simply expand rosters.

Five more players mean five more salaries.

Unless the salary cap changes with the roster limit, teams would still be working with the same pool of money. A bigger roster filled with minimum-salary players doesn't automatically solve a depth problem.

There are other ways the league could approach it.

Additional roster spots could be treated differently against the cap. Injured reserve rules could become more forgiving for shorter-term injuries. The NFL could expand the number of players available on game day without making a dramatic change to the 53-man roster.

A second bye week deserves to be part of the discussion, too.

There probably isn't one fix because there isn't one problem. Teams need enough players, enough money to keep those players, and enough recovery time to make the whole thing useful.

The 17-game season has been around long enough that it already feels normal. An 18th game wouldn't feel normal immediately.

That would potentially put a Super Bowl team on the field 22 times between the regular season and postseason. Think about that from the perspective of an offensive lineman who rarely leaves the field.

That's a lot of snaps before even counting practices.

If the NFL eventually goes there, adding another bye would make sense. So would another look at roster limits.

The league could also force teams to adjust naturally. Coaches might become more willing to rotate players. General managers might spend differently, putting more money into the 30th through 45th players on the roster instead of concentrating so much of it at the top.

But there is a reason that hasn't happened already.

A coach isn't going to take his best tackle off the field in a three-point game because he might need him four months later. That's a nice idea until the backup gives up a sack and the team loses.

The NFL created a longer season, but coaches still have to survive it one Sunday at a time.

The 17-Game Season Isn't Going Back to 16

Another regular-season game means another weekend people watch football. It means another home game every other year for each team. It means another television window the NFL can sell.

Sixteen games aren't coming back. We will have a 17-game season for the foreseeable future.

So the interesting discussion isn't whether the league should undo the 17-game season. It's whether everything surrounding the schedule should continue operating the same way.

The NFL has changed plenty in the name of player safety. Rules have changed. Equipment has improved. Practice time has been reduced and regulated.

Maybe roster size and rest eventually belong on that list. No rule is going to keep every player healthy. Neither will five additional roster spots, nor another bye week. Football doesn't work that way.

But there's a big gap between eliminating injuries and giving teams a better chance of handling them. Right now, too many seasons eventually become a test of who still has enough healthy players left.

Maybe the 17-game season isn't actually too long. Maybe 53 players aren't enough for it. That's a different argument, and it becomes a much bigger one if the NFL ever adds an 18th game.

The league doesn't need to tear up its entire roster system. A few more spots could help. So could another bye, different injured reserve rules, or more flexibility with the players available on Sundays.

There will always be attrition in football. Nobody is changing that.

But the NFL changed the length of its season five years ago from 16 games to a 17-game season. Eventually, it may have to change the roster built to play it.

articles.title: Grading Joey Porter Jr. Blockbuster NFL Trade Between Cowboys and Steelers
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have established a trade pipeline with the Dallas Cowboys. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. will reunite with former Steelers teammates Broderick Jones, whom Dallas acquired about a month ago, and George Pickens.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have established a trade pipeline with the Dallas Cowboys. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. will reunite with former Steelers teammates Broderick Jones, whom Dallas acquired about a month ago, and George Pickens.

According to ESPN's Todd Archer and Brooke Pryor , Dallas sent Pittsburgh a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for Porter.

Porter has dealt with a back injury, and not so coincidentally, a contract dispute since training camp.

Early in July, Chris Mack of the Kaboly and Mack podcast said there's a "belief" that Porter wanted an extension averaging around $30 million. That sounds reasonable, given that cornerbacks Christian Gonzalez and Devon Witherspoon, who also entered the league in 2023, signed new deals averaging $33.75 million and $33 million, respectively.

Instead of giving Porter an extension, Pittsburgh dealt him, which is a move many saw coming because of how the franchise does business.

So, let's break down the short- and long-term layers of this trade to assess these teams' defensive outlook and Porter's future. Here are the immediate grades.

The Dallas Cowboys left Rio de Janeiro embarrassed, having allowed a 27-yard completion and a game-winning 56-yard field goal to the Baltimore Ravens in just seven seconds. While you can blame defensive coordinator Christian Parker for a poor play call after the touchback, the Cowboys absolutely need a lead cornerback.

Dallas has allowed seven passing touchdowns in three weeks. Cornerback DaRon Bland is allowing a passer rating of 108.8 in coverage. Cobie Durant didn't suit up last week because of a hamstring injury.

When Joey Porter Jr. is ready to take the field, he'll be the Cowboys' clear-cut No. 1 cover man on the boundary. Through three seasons in Pittsburgh, he recorded 31 pass breakups, three interceptions and allowed a 57.2 passer rating in coverage. Touted for his man coverage ability out of Penn State, he can shadow lead wide receivers and force quarterbacks to target secondary pass-catchers.

Dallas should be far better in pass coverage going forward, as long as Porter's supposed back injury clears up.

Beyond a significant upgrade at cornerback, the Cowboys didn't even give up a premium 2027 draft pick, which is a major plus with all the buzz around potential first- and second-round prospects.

Lastly, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , Dallas isn't expected to sign Porter to a new deal, which was a sticking point in the cornerback's divorce from the Steelers.

The Cowboys get an established and ascending player, keep their top 2027 picks and won't go through the headache of contract negotiations, which contributed to Porter's recent inactivity in Pittsburgh. This is a slam dunk move for Dallas' front office.

As some may know, the Steelers are notoriously stingy with guaranteed money, and they don't negotiate with players during the regular season.

While Steelers general managers before Omar Khan have abided by these guidelines, The Athletic's Mike DeFabo pointed the finger at him anyway.

" While most of the public criticism has been pointed at Porter, the Steelers should not be absolved of blame. Khan has a history of letting negotiations linger to the last minute . That comes along with two long-standing (and, arguably, outdated) front-office policies: The Steelers rarely give out guaranteed money and they don't negotiate contracts during the season."

With $11.6 million in cap space and projected to be $9.2 million over the limit in 2027, Pittsburgh has to be conservative with contracts, but this isn't the one.

The Steelers have a veteran-led roster with 42-year-old quarterback Aaron Rodgers and several defensive players like T.J. Watt, Cameron Heyward and Jalen Ramsey in their 30s. Khan has a win-now squad that needs young talent to stay competitive long term.

On the one hand, the Steelers signed defensive lineman Keeanu Benton, outside linebacker Nick Herbig, wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr., running back Jaylen Warren and tight end Darnell Washington to extensions. They're all up-and-coming talent or in their prime.

Yet, Khan couldn't make room on the books for the team's top cornerback. Barring an unreasonable contract request, the Steelers should've prioritized Porter's deal over the players they extended this offseason.

To make matters worse, the Steelers didn't get a player in return who plays the same position as Porter or a pick that's likely to help them within the next year. Jamel Dean and Asante Samuel Jr. could be a decent cornerback duo, but the former has missed 12 games since 2023 and the latter has allowed two touchdowns and a passer rating of 135.4 so far this season.

In the short term, this is a major blunder for the Steelers .

Porter may benefit from a change of scenery. The Cowboys have a more potent offense than the Steelers' 26th-ranked scoring unit. So his defensive contributions may stand out more when opponents force the ball downfield while playing from behind. Dallas is also less likely to waste a solid defensive outing with a low-scoring output.

However, Porter may be in the same contract situation he was in Pittsburgh.

As previously noted, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that Porter will play out the season on his current deal.

So, does Porter's back injury clear up quickly as he bets on himself, hoping Dallas rewards him in the next offseason? Did he just want a split from the Steelers, knowing that the Cowboys weren't going to sign him to an immediate extension either?

In a contract year, Porter didn't get what he wanted and still has to prove himself worthy of a lucrative deal that puts him on a similar pay scale as cornerbacks Devon Witherspoon and Christian Gonzalez. And there's no guarantee that the Cowboys will extend him. Like George Pickens this year, they could franchise-tag him.

Perhaps Porter's contract negotiations with the Steelers soured their relationship beyond repair, and he preferred to chase a new deal elsewhere. Still, this isn't the best possible outcome for a player who held out for a new deal.

Team salary cap information provided by Over the Cap .

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.

articles.title: Mike Tomlin shows off incredibly detailed Minecraft city he built when he was coaching Steelers
articles.summary: Mike Tomlin put a lot of thought into lighting and interior design... really.
articles.body:
For all his success, former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin received his fair share of criticism during his 19-year run in the position. But one thing he could never be condemned for was his attention to detail, a trait that apparently extends far beyond his football life.

Turns out, while Tomlin was leading the Steelers to winning records he was also building an elaborately detailed city in the video game Minecraft. Tomlin revealed that tidbit during a September interview on the "Today Show," saying he spent 12 years planning and building the city.

It seemed too outlandish to be true. Was a future Hall of Fame coach spending his down time painstakingly building a city in a video game popular with a much younger generation?

Well, Tomlin gave fans that answer Wednesday night with a tour of his elaborate city. It was … pretty incredible.

Prior to showing off his city, Tomlin revealed that he started playing Minecraft as a way to connect with his kids. Even though his kids have left the game behind, Tomlin has continued to add to his city. During his interview with the "Today Show," Tomlin said his kids — who are grown now — encourage him to show off the city every time they visit.

And if the above clip is any indication, they had many, many reasons to encourage their dad to make his interest public. Tomlin clearly put a lot of thought and care into the project, explaining that he wanted to build the city around a large body of water.

From there, he kept making additions … like, lots of them. Tomlin showed off therapy rooms, public restrooms, a baseball stadium and glass elevators, among many, many other details . Tomlin also gave his thoughts on interior decorating, lighting fixtures and bedroom furniture in his video. No, really.

Tomlin's full video — which he posted on his YouTube page — came in under 20 minutes, which was nowhere near enough time for him to show off his entire city. Fans hoping to see more are in luck, though. Tomlin teased future episodes in which he planned to show off other aspects of his city.

Now that he's no longer coaching, Tomlin presumably has even more time to keep adding to his Minecraft city. While many assumed Tomlin's time away from the NFL would be short-lived, Wednesday's unveiling may have paved the way for Tomlin to turn in a lucrative second act as one of the biggest Minecraft streamers around. That sounds a lot less stressful than taking on another head-coaching job in the NFL, especially for someone already as accomplished as Tomlin.
